full_judgment:
Under challenge in this Rule are the judgment and decree dated 12-10-95 passed by the learned 3rd Senior Assistant Judge and SCC Judge, Dhaka in SCC Case No.24 of 1992 dismissing the suit, giving rise to the filing of this revisional application under section 25 of the Small Causes Court Act and the issuance of this Rule. 

 2. The plaintiff (landlord) Jahanara Hasan is the petitioner before this court. She instituted SCC Case No.92 of 1990 for ejectment of defendant Nos. l and 2 (tenant opposite parties) ie. Md Nazrul Islam and Md. Sirajul Islam, two of her full brothers, from the suit premises, in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court and SCC Dhaka. The suit was re-numbered as SCC suit No.24 of 1992. 

 3. The case of the landlord/landlady, in short, is that the defendant No.1, Nazrul Islam was a monthly tenant in the suit premises under terms and conditions laid down in the tenancy agreement dated 1-3-83; the terms and conditions in 'the said agreement inter alia were that the tenant without consent of the landlord would not sub-let the suit premises and the tenancy would terminate for non payment of rent for consecutive three months; that the defendant No.1 in violation of those terms set up defendant No.2 Siraj Mia as a sub-tenant in the suit premises, and that he defaulted in paying  the rent with effect from April, 1989 'to July, 1989 and filed Rent Control Case No.67 of 1989 in the court of the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court and Rent Controller, Dhaka by depositing the rent with effect from August, 1989 alleging, inter alia, that the landlord, landlady (his full sister) did not collect rent for the month of August, 1989 in time and also did not give them the receipts against payment of rent for the months of April to July, 1989 although several approaches were made to that effect. The plaintiff landlord appeared in the said rent control case and denied all the allegations made in the said case but did not oppose the prayer for depositing the rent without any prejudice being caused to her. The rent controller by order dated 31-10-92 allowed the tenant opposite party to deposit rent without passing any order on the prayer as to non-issuance of the rent receipts by the landlord. It was also stated by the landlord that she required the suit premises for her own use; that proper notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was also served on the defendant for vacating the suit premises but the tenant did not vacate and hence Ilk-suit. 

 4. The defendant opposite parties contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint. They contended inter alia that the defendant No.1 is not a defaulter; he is a tenant of the plaintiff in the said premises and has been regularly paying rent to the plaintiff; that the plaintiff despite regular receipt of monthly rent was in the habit of issuing receipts for few months at a time because they happened to be the full brothers of the plaintiff; that they duly paid rent for the months of April, May, June, and July, 1989 but the landlord despite repeated demands did not issue them the rent receipts; that upon offer of the rent for August, 1989 the landlord refused to accept the same and hence the defendant No.1 filed Rent Control Case, No.67 of 1989 in the court of the 3rd Assistant Judge and Rent Controller, Dhaka. for depositing the rent and was allowed to deposit rent without prejudice to the plaintiff landlord by order dated 31-10-92; that since then the defendant No.1 has been depositing rent to therent controller; that the defendant No.2 is not a sub-tenant, He is also a full brother of defendant No.1 as well as of the plaintiff landlord. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are members of a joint family running the business jointly in the suit premises. That the plaintiff landlord does not require the suit premises for her personal use and in the circumstances the suit IS liable to be dismissed. The Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka by judgment and order dated 12-10-85 dismissed the suit holding, inter alia, that the defendant No.1 is not a defaulter; that he has not set up a sub-tenant in the suit premises and that the landlord does not require the premises for her own use and thus being aggrieved the landlord moved this court and obtained the instant Rule. . 

 5. Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner, submits that the fact that the defendant is a defaulter is apparent from the deposition of DW 1 Serajul Islam who stated in his cross examination that he paid rent. for the months of November  and December, 1990 in court on 1-1-91 and for the months of November' and December, 1993 on 1-1-94, Me Md Azizul Hoque, learned Advocate appearing for the tenant opposite parties, argued that the month of December is the annual vacation for the Judges Court and it.re-opened on the 1st of January and that is why the rent for the month of November could not be paid on the 15th of December, but as soon as the court re-opened he paid rent on the 1st of January. Mr. Knondker next submits that Ext.3 which is a letter dated 21-6-89 written by defendant No.1 Nazrul Islam to the plaintiff landlord stating that because of his illness (major operation) he was. not in a position to carry on the business and, as such, he is entrusting his brother Serajul Islam with the task of carrying on the business and from now on the said Serajul Islam will pay the rent and all other charges which, according to Mr Khondaker, is nothing but sub-letting the premises to defendant NO.2 but from Ext. 3 I find that this is a simple communication of defendant NO.1 to his sister is plaintiff as to his inability to run the business himself. The defendant No.1 is deriving no pecuniary benefit from the change of management of the business and the most important aspect is that had it been a case of sub-letting, as alleged by the plaintiff, the defendant No.1 instead of communicating this letter to the landlord would have kept quiet. The trial Court came to a finding that Ext.3 can not be said to be a sub-lease. The next point urged by Mr. Khondker is that for the months of April, 1989 to July, 1989 the defendant No.1 remained a defaulter. I find from the deposition of PW 1 Jahanara Hasan, who is the full sister of defendant Nos.l and 2, that she has been collecting rent herself since 1987 and prior to that her sister-in-law used to collect rent. She further stated that rent for the suit premises was some time paid by defendant No.1 himself and some time it was paid through defendant Serajul Islam. She also• admitted that the defendant No.1 has been running the business in the suit premises since 1982. In her cross examination the plaintiff denied the fact that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are full brothers although it appears fro in the plaint the she herself and the defendant Nos. l and 2 are the children of late Nasiruddin Ahmed of village Sadahpur, Thana Nowabgonj, District Dhaka and for telling this lie the trial Court disbelieved her statement that Serajul Islam did not pay to her the rent for the months of April to July, 1989 and that she did not willfully issue the rent receipt. The trial Court also considered the fact that in the House Rent Case No. 67 of 1989 the House Rent Controller by order dated 31-10-92 allowed the defendant to deposit rent in court. The trial Court believed the testimony of DW 1 Serajul Islam that he paid rent for the months of April to July, 1989 at a time since a practice had developed between the parties for paying and receiving the rents for several months at a time, the trial Court disbelieved the plaintiff PW 1 on the ground that in her cross-examination she stated that Serajul (Defendant No.1) sometimes used to pay rents on behalf of defendant No.1 Nazrul Islam then said I have never seen Serajul Islam in the shop, then again she said I do not know how Serajul Islam came in the shop. This coupled with the fact that the plaintiff denied the fact that. Serajul Islam is the brother of Nazrul Islam although all the 3 are the children of Nasiruddin Ahmed and having observed the demeanour of PW 1 while deposing in court, the learned Judge rightly disbelieved her and accepted the testimony of DW 1 Serajul Islam as regards payment of rent for the months of April to July, 1989.
